Hi Dylan,

Thanks for agreeing to help with our Privacy Impact Assessment. Please find attached our standard PIA template (MediNova_PIA_Template_2026.xlsx). We need fields completed for sections covering:
- data flows and transfer locations (including SCCs)
- categories of data processed (HIPAA / special category / pseudonymised)
- technical and organisational controls (encryption at rest/in transit, key management, access control)
- retention schedules and deletion procedures
- processor-subprocessor relationships and subprocessors list

A few clarifying questions up front:
1) Can you confirm whether Redwood acts strictly as a processor under our DPA for the service in scope?
2) For EU customer data, do you rely on SCCs or have any other transfer mechanism?
3) For access logs and admin activity, what retention window is available for evidence export?

Our internal timeline: legal & privacy team would like a completed draft by July 16, and a short walkthrough call if possible next week.

Attachment: MediNova_PIA_Template_2026.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

Elena —

Thanks for the template and the timeline. We're happy to take the lead on a draft. Quick answers to your questions:
- Processor role: Yes, for hosted Redwood API usage we operate as a processor per the standard Redwood DPA. We can flag the exact clause references in the completed template.
- Transfers: We use EU Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) for transfers where applicable and can point to the executed SCC language in our DPA.
- Access logs retention: We can export admin activity / access logs covering the last 90 days by default; for longer retention we can provide a one-off export where permitted by contract.

Action plan:
1) I'll coordinate a short walkthrough with Security (Evelyn) and Legal (Mina) — proposed times: Mon 13 Jul 10:00 CEST or Tue 14 Jul 09:00 CEST.
2) We'll produce a draft completed template and a redacted evidence bundle (SOC2 summary, SCC statement, and sample logs) by Thu 15 Jul.

Attached: redwood-pia-guidance-2026.pdf (internal guidance — high level answers to common PIA questions).

Hi Elena and team,

Thanks for sending the template. Per our call this morning (notes below), we've populated the primary sections and attached a draft completed workbook. Highlights and items that need your confirmation:

1) Roles and responsibilities- Redwood confirms processor role for hosted API use under our standard DPA. We'll populate clause references in the template (see workbook tab: Legal Clauses).

2) Transfers & safeguards- We rely on the EU SCCs for transfers; executed language is available in our DPA and we have a signed Annex covering subprocessors. See attached: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (controls summary) and sccs-execution-statement.txt (short statement on SCCs).

3) Data categories and lawful basis- For customers processing special category data (health), we emphasize that customers are the controller and must ensure lawful basis / consent. We have controls to support confidentiality: AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.2+ in transit, customer-managed KMS options for Dedicated/Private deployments (not available on shared hosted tiers).

4) Retention and deletion- Default log retention: 90 days for system logs; audit trail exports available on request for contractually agreed windows. Data deletion: we support retention windows and provide deletion APIs; full environment wipes are available for Dedicated/Private.

5) Subprocessors- We maintain a dynamic subprocessors list; snapshot attached in the workbook (tab: Subprocessors). We also created a recommended response note in the template for you to include in your DPIA.

Attachments submitted via secure Drive:
- redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (SOC2 scope & control summary)
- sccs-execution-statement.txt (how we implement SCCs and an executed reference)
- draft_medinova_pia_completed.xlsx (draft answers, redacted where needed)

Next steps we propose:
- Please review the draft workbook and indicate any requested redactions or additions by Thu 15 Jul EOD.
- If you require longer log exports (beyond 90 days), let us know the legal justification and timeframe so we can coordinate with infra for an export.

On the call, Dylan flagged one narrow question around: whether MediNova expects Redwood to sign Data Transfer Impact Assessment outputs — typically Redwood provides factual inputs and evidence, while customers record the resulting risk decisions. Happy to discuss that operational model if you prefer a different approach.

Regards,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Security & Compliance Engineer | Redwood Inference
